feature: Risk Register (#2993, Feature #1487) -- the real customer-facing Risk Register page in the rebuilt artifacts/portal (/risk-register), wired to GET /api/portal/risk-register, GET /api/portal/policy-decisions, POST /api/portal/risk-register/:rbdId/accept, and GET /api/portal/risk-register/rbd/:rbdId/versions -- see docs/risk-register-contract-pack.md. No fixture module: every row on screen comes from these endpoints. #3058 wired the whole-document viewer + drawn-signature capture (GET .../versions/:versionUid/document, POST .../versions/:versionUid/sign) that this manifest's DOC steps below cover.
notes: #3058 -- no msp_rbd_versions row exists anywhere in the local/testbed DB (confirmed via direct SELECT this session), so the document/sign happy path (a real rendered WireRbdDocument, a real 201 sign) is NOT driven end-to-end here -- rendering one needs a real MSP staff createdByUserId via the separate msp-rbd-versions.ts route, which is out of this manifest's scope. What IS driven: the scoped-404 guard on both new routes for a version that does not exist (DOC1/DOC2, idempotent), and the honest 'No document prepared yet' empty state rendering for real on a row with zero captured versions (UI8). If an MSP-rendered + customer-signable version is ever seeded for the testbed tenant, extend this manifest with the real document-render + sign-and-verify-409-on-resubmit path the same way A3's write-once guard was proven (see that note) rather than leaving this gap silently uncovered.

WHAT THIS COVERS: the real read shapes (risks[]/decisions[] arrays, the two fields this build added to the wire -- WireAcceptance.status and WireRisk.obligation, both real DB columns that existed but were not previously served), the write-once accept guard (409 on an already-accepted row), the 404 on a nonexistent rbdId, and that the per-RBD version-history read answers cleanly even when no version has ever been captured (empty array, not an error).

WHY NO HAPPY-PATH ACCEPT IS DRIVEN HERE: an acceptance is PERMANENT -- the route refuses a second one with 409 -- so a step that successfully accepts a risk would pass exactly once and then poison every subsequent run of this manifest. A real accept WAS proven end-to-end in-session against a locally-built copy of this exact commit (RBD-2026-103, seeded via lib/db/migrations/manual/2026-08-21-portal-v2-risk-register-testbed-seed.sql): 201 with the new status:'active' field present, an immediate second attempt refused 409, then the row was reset via direct SQL back to its seeded pending_signature/Open state so this manifest's own A3/A4 guards stay true on every run. That sequence is deliberately not a manifest step, for the same non-idempotency reason.

AUTH CORE HAS LANDED (#2991, Feature #1648, #3061) -- login.tsx now ships real #email/#password inputs and a login-submit testid (verified this session, login.tsx:230/248/257), so this manifest drives a real login instead of only asserting the pre-auth honest empty state. This note previously said no login form existed yet; that premise is stale and is corrected here.

WHY NO HAPPY-PATH ACCEPT SUBMIT IS DRIVEN VIA THE UI EITHER (same reasoning as the API-level A3/A4 guards above): an acceptance is permanent and the accept dialog's own submit would poison every subsequent run. The uiSteps below open the risk-accept-name/-statement/-confirm/-sign controls on an already-accepted seeded row (RBD-2026-104) to prove the real controls render, without ever clicking risk-accept-sign-<id>.

SEEDED TEST DATA: the testbed tenant's real register content is seeded demonstration data (lib/db/migrations/manual/2026-08-21-portal-v2-risk-register-testbed-seed.sql, idempotent via ON CONFLICT), not organic assessment output -- the READ path, the SCOPING and the ACCEPT write path it exercises are real. Re-run that file if A1/A2 below drift.
ENV VARS (BuildConsole -> Settings -> Test Environment Variables): DEPLOY_URL, TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL / TEST_PORTAL_PASSWORD.

apiTests.name: SETUP -- log in as the designated testbed portal account; extract the bearer.
A1 -- the customer-scoped register answers 200 with an array.
A1b -- take the first real row's id, the value UI3 below proves reached the DOM.
A2 -- the policy-decisions view of the same table also answers 200 with an array.
A2b -- take the first real decision's id, the value UI7 below proves reached the DOM (decisions[] is derived from risks[], so this is the same rbdId shape as A1b).
A3 -- accepting an already-accepted seeded risk (RBD-2026-104, always signed by the seed) is refused 409, proving the write-once guard, idempotently re-runnable.
A4 -- a nonexistent rbdId 404s exactly like a real risk belonging to another tenant would (no ID-probing signal).
A5 -- a version history read for an RBD with no captured version answers 200 with an empty array, not an error (#1512 surface, no version ever rendered for the seeded rows).
DOC1 (#3058, sessionTag rbd-document) -- GET .../document for a versionUid that does not exist 404s scoped exactly like one belonging to another tenant would, not a 500.
DOC2 (#3058, sessionTag rbd-document) -- POST .../sign for a versionUid that does not exist also 404s, idempotently re-runnable (no state written on a 404).
